column2: Creeley leaves for San Francisco

BMC Bulletin, vol. 12, no. 1, a fifteen-page mimeograph (“The American Language,” “The Western Tradition,” “Pre-Homeric Literature and Culture,” “Theocritus”), mainly for the V.A.; the work in fact tutorial
Robert Duncan returns (with Jess Collins) in early summer 1956; the poem “Old Son” on Olson
Months of rehearsals of Robert Duncan's Medea, written as the rehearsals went on, directed by Wes Huss, with Don Mixon (Jason), Eric Weinberger, John Wieners

Early fall 1956: Olson, who no longer wants to teach, and Huss decide in an Asheville café to close the college; alternatives set aside (Tony Landreau's mobile university and Olson's scheme, Channel 2's “University of the Air,” a skyscraper floor in Manhattan rented by Paul Williams)
Dispersal within thirty days: Fiore to New York, Huss and the Medea troupe with Duncan to San Francisco; Olson stays for the liquidation

Olson stays about six months with Betty Kaiser and their son: sale of the remaining property, John Andrew Rice's library (partly taken by Nell Rice, the rest sold to North Carolina Wesleyan), upkeep of the graves of Jalowetz and Max Dehn; then leaves for Gloucester (“Now ARISE”)
In San Francisco, the Medea troupe breaks up; the bar of Knute Stiles and Leo Krikorian; Ginsberg and Corso on the “Black Mountain people” (1956 interview with Lawrence Lipton)
Jonathan Williams crisscrosses the country in his father's station wagon loaded with books (Jargon, Golden Goose, City Lights, Grove, New Directions)
Daniel Dixon, “Ssss, Boom, Phffft!,” Pageant, on the closing

The Black Mountain Review no. 7 (the last, 240 pp.): Ginsberg contributing editor, “America,” Kerouac, Snyder, Whalen, McClure, Burroughs (“William Lee,” Naked Lunch), Hubert Selby Jr.; a negative review of Howl by Rumaker
Duberman receives the Bancroft Prize for Charles Francis Adams, 1807–1886
Buckminster Fuller receives an honorary doctorate from Harvard; a preparatory session with Arthur Penn at a dinner
The former faculty members' lawsuit for back salaries essentially ends (correspondence until 1967)
Duberman's documentary play In White America receives the Vernon Rice-Drama Desk Award
Betty Kaiser, Olson's second wife, killed in a car accident
Duberman's James Russell Lowell nominated for the National Book Award
Robert Moore's mimeographed questionnaire for an exhibition on Black Mountain (Jonathan Williams's reply)
John Sinclair, from the Detroit House of Detention, on Olson in whe’re (summer 1966)
Duberman's research: the BMC archives at the State Archives in Raleigh (~100,000 documents, ~10,000 photocopies), hundreds of recorded interviews, funding from the Rockefeller Foundation
Duberman begins the book; goes through the ~100,000 documents at the State Archives in Raleigh and the recorded interviews
A dinner at which James Leo Herlihy (a BMC student in the late 1940s) tells Duberman, who had never heard of it, about the college: the origin of the book
Duberman spends three days with Erwin and Trudi Straus in Lexington (Kentucky); notes in his motel
Duberman writes the first three chapters, then sets the manuscript aside for a year
Three-volume reprint of The Black Mountain Review by AMS Press, introduction by Creeley
Death of Charles Olson in early January 1970, before Duberman could meet him
Duberman takes up the manuscript again

Duberman's diary on his unstructured seminar “American Radicalism” at Princeton (September 17, 22, 24, 29, October 6 and 8, November 19, 1970, with Bill Caspary; graduate seminar on Oneida, February 16, 1971)
Duberman receives an award from the National Academy of Arts and Letters
Duberman resigns from Princeton
First edition of Black Mountain: An Exploration in Community by E. P. Dutton & Co. (New York)
Anchor Books paperback edition (Anchor Press / Doubleday, Garden City), ISBN 0-385-07059-4 — the edition indexed here
Death of Ralph Reed Lounsbury, professor of government, public law, and history
Ted Dreier and Robert Wunsch leave on a business trip for the college
Admission of John Ormai, from the Yale School of Fine Arts
Arrival of Donald Stein, transferring from Stanford
High school students meet college representatives: Black Mountain College invited (New Trier, Winnetka, Illinois)
High school students meet college representatives: Black Mountain College invited (Bethesda, Chevy Chase, Maryland)
High school students meet college representatives: Black Mountain College invited (Pingry, Elizabeth, New Jersey)
High school students meet college representatives: Black Mountain College invited (Fieldston, Spuyten Duyvil, New York)
Preliminary plans of the Lake Eden building (Gropius and Breuer) ready for publication: general plans and views

General meeting: the rector, on behalf of the Board of Fellows, announces the resignation of J. A. Rice, effective at the end of the academic year; Robert Wunsch reads a statement: Rice has asked to leave in order to devote himself entirely to writing
Robert Wunsch speaks at the college conference of the Western Arts Association, Cincinnati
Ted Dreier at Bolton Landing, Lake George (N.Y.), until August 23, then at Lake Eden
Death of Frank Nacke, Student Moderator and member of the Board of Fellows, in the Lake Eden flood
End of guest reservations at the Lake Eden inn (run by Charles Lindsley and Morton Steinau)
Memorial service for Frank Nacke
Benefit concert: piano recital by Germaine and Claude Monteux at the home of Mr. and Mrs. Joseph B. Jamieson
Benefit concert: soprano, two flutes, and piano (Jane Mayhall Katz, Claude Monteux, and two friends) at the home of Mr. and Mrs. J. Malcolm Forbes
The magazine supplement of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch publishes John Stix's color photographs of the construction
Benefit concert: second program by Jane Mayhall Katz and Claude Monteux at the home of Mr. and Mrs. Richard Hubbard
Benefit concert at the home of Mr. and Mrs. John P. Carr
Visit by the anthropologist Paul Radin: a formal lecture and a series of talks and discussions on his theories (week of March 5)
George W. Hendrickson graduates from Black Mountain College in theater (Dramatics)
Will Hamlin's article comparing Antioch and Black Mountain in The Antiochian
Visitors' Week: lecture by Lewis Mumford (announced in January)
Nathan Rosen among the speakers at the annual meeting of the American Physical Society (May 1-3)
The college's equipment and belongings moved to Lake Eden (last week of May)
Work Camp: a series of four discussions on the economic problems of the South
Death of Mark Dreier, age nine, son of Theodore and Barbara Dreier, in a car accident near the Lake Eden dam
Brief memorial service for Mark Dreier for his friends
Charles Lindsley, professor of chemistry, leaves for a national defense research position at the University of Virginia
President Roosevelt speaks on the radio on “The Bill of Rights”
Derek Bovingdon completes his basic training at Fort Knox (Kentucky)
February exhibition at the Boston Art Museum, with paintings by Harrison Begay, a Native American student at the college the year before
Derek Bovingdon passes the Air Corps examinations
Bob Wunsch leaves for Newport News (Virginia): four days of work with the teachers of the Black high school
Ted Dreier leaves for New York on a business trip for the college
Arrival of Ted Dreier and his parents, Mr. and Mrs. H. E. Dreier
Publication of Paul Radin's book Indians of South America (Doubleday, Doran)
Arrival of Mrs. Eduard Denfey, Renate's mother
George Hendrickson drafted into the field artillery
19th State Dramatic Festival (Chapel Hill): Frances Kuntz wins first prize for costume plates (The Highbrow Ladies) and the highest award for her costumes
Return of the delegation to the Southern Conference on Human Welfare (Nashville)
Bob Wunsch at Lincoln-Grant High School in Covington (Kentucky)
Margot Bergmann successfully operated on
Bob Wunsch at the Webster-Davis Laboratory School near Petersburg (Virginia)
Bob Wunsch returns from his last 1941-42 tour of Black high schools
Announced publication of Peter Bergmann's book on the theory of relativity (Prentice-Hall)
Notice on the bulletin board: students to register for sugar rationing
Peter Bergmann expected back (Wednesday or Thursday)
Peter Bergmann receives his naturalization papers: a citizen of the United States
Bob Babcock, on leave from the college, takes a position with Foreign Funds Control: arrives in Washington
Letter from Antioch College to Robert Wunsch (reply to his letter of May 7) in support of Black Mountain College; Louis Adamic, who knows BMC, was at Antioch the week before
Swarthmore College announces that it will accept Black Mountain College students on the same terms as those from other institutions
John Evarts enlists in the army; sent to the Fort Jackson (S.C.) induction center, rejected for a hernia, he returns to the college

Frank Porter Graham, president of the University of North Carolina, writes to the Secretaries of the Navy and of War: the university accepts BMC students on the college's recommendation, although it is not yet accredited
John Evarts operated on in an Asheville hospital; convalescence at the college
Four pages of PIC magazine devoted to the college
Death of J. Richard Carpenter, Assistant Professor of Biology, at Duke Memorial Hospital
Robert Wunsch speaks to the summer students and the work campers about the Negro problem in America (socioeconomic aspects)
Birth of Robert Shillingford Babcock Jr., son of Robert and Alice Ann Babcock
First Southern Training Institute of the Textile Workers Union of America (CIO), on the college grounds
Deadline: corridors of the Studies Building and the lodges entirely cleared of trunks and boxes (state fire regulations)
Community meeting on the committees needed for the year and their functions
Jimmy Jamieson leaves for a Civilian Public Service camp, probably in New Hampshire
The list of committees and their purposes presented to the community for review and discussion
Arrival of Roland Boyden for a five-day visit
Arrival of John A. Collett, a new student from Los Angeles
John Evarts enlists in the army (second attempt)
